To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
haloperidol increases and clozapine does not alter the percentage of perforate synapses in the rat brain.
haloperidol increases the density of perforation synapses in the dorsolateral region of the caudate and that the increase is reversed by drug withdrawal.
haloperidol treatment for 2 weeks increases the density of perforations at synapses in the dorsolateral striatum, but not in nucleus accumbens.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of haliperidol and clozepine on the morphology of synapses within three DA-rich regions, the caudate and nucleus accumbens and the medial prefrontal (cortex) and whether these changes are related to the incidence of EPS and/or TD.
the effects of halperidol and clozpine on the morphology of synapses within three DA-rich areas of the brain.
the effect of chronic administration of neuroleptics and other psychotropic drugs on the density and ultrastructure of “perforations” at postsynaptic sites within the striatum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clozapine is not as potent as haloperidol in inducing EPS and TD because it does not increase the number of perforant synapses in the DA-rich regions that we have studied.
the effect of haloperidole is to increase the percentage of perforate synapses in the dorsolateral region of caudate nucleus, but that clozapine does not have this effect.
the increase in the number perforated synapses observed with haloperidole is associated with a downregulation of DA receptors in the caude nucleus and MPCx.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perforated synapses can be used as a sensitive indicator for monitoring changes in DA receptor sensitivity.

1) perforated synapses are sensitive to changes in DA neurotransmission, 2) perforated synapse density is a sensitive index of DA receptor activation, 3) clozapine is not a DA agonist in the striatum, and 4) the effects of clozpine on perforated synapse number in MPCx is related to its ability to depolarize the A9 DA neurons.
haloperidol increases perforated synapse density in the dorsolateral region of the caudate but not nucleus accumbens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
haloperidol, but not clozapine, causes an increase in perforated synapses that is correlated with an increased density of D-2 receptors and a decrease in 5-HT2 receptors.
clozapine does not cause the increase in perforated synapses seen with haloperidole and may be a better treatment option for patients with schizophrenia.
the density of perforations in the post-synaptic membrane of synapses is altered by the drugs we studied, and the changes are region-specific.
